name: Signature extractor
pitch: Pull phone numbers and addresses from email signatures and put them in a spreadsheet.
instructions: Extract phone numbers and physical addresses from the person's email signatures and list them in a spreadsheet. Start by reading the inbox and finding messages that have a signature block at the bottom. For each message, look at the last 1500 characters and pull out any line that looks like a phone number (digits and plus signs, or a local format) and any line that looks like a street address (number, street name, city, postcode). Put each find into a table with columns: name, phone, address. If a signature has no phone or no address, leave that cell blank. When all signatures are processed, show the table to the person and ask if they want it saved as a CSV file. If the inbox is empty or no signatures are found, say so and offer to look at a specific folder or search for messages from a particular sender.

examples.ask: can you pull addresses from my mail
examples.does: read the last messages, list any addresses found in a table, and ask if the person wants a CSV

examples.ask: i have a new job, sort my contacts
examples.does: scan recent signatures, build a table of names and phones, show it, wait for go-ahead to save

examples.ask: my signatures are messy, clean them up
examples.does: extract what is there, tell the person if anything looks wrong, do not invent missing data

readme:
# Signature extractor
Extracts phone numbers and addresses from email signatures into a spreadsheet.

What it does: Reads the person's mail, finds signature blocks, pulls out contact details and lists them in a table. The person can then save the table as a CSV.

What it needs: Access to read mail, ability to write a CSV file, and a table display tool.

What it will not do: It will not guess phone numbers or addresses that are not clearly in the signature. It will not save anything without the person's go-ahead.
